name: the viewer image back in flow
why: Out of flow is what keeps the image from sizing the stage. In flow (here in a block stage) it sits at the stage's top-left instead of centred in the frame, and in the old grid stage its natural height stretched the row past the stage and overflow: hidden cut the bottom off (org/viewer.org #1).
grep: fitted, the whole image is inside the stage

name: the image box is not sized to the fit
why: Without the px size the CSS max-width/max-height fallback still fits a LARGE image, but shows the thumbnail at its natural 250 px, so the large image jumps in at a different size.
grep: the thumbnail is shown at the size

name: the top/bottom gutter is not read
why: The frame is the stage minus the gutters read from --mb-artv-gx/--mb-artv-gy; without them the fitted image touches the stage's top and bottom. Only the FIT shows it: the geometry stays self-consistent, so the zoomed pan reaches exactly the stage's edge, which the per-edge test allows. (Before the extras branch it was the other way round: the CSS max-height clamped the box, hiding it from the fit and making the pan over-pan. _artViewerFit() now lifts that clamp, since a quarter-turned box can be wider than the frame.)
grep: fitted, the whole image is inside the stage

name: the narrow layout keeps the wide gutters
why: Below 760 px the media query sets the smaller gutters on the stage, and the JS reads them from there; without it the narrow image is fitted 4 px further in than the frame.

name: the pan follows the mouse only over the stage
why: The original handler's guard. A fast move off the stage lands outside it in ONE event, so the pan stopped short of the edge (org/viewer.org #1, cause B).

edits.find:
st.ptr = { x: e.clientX, y: e.clientY };
        if (!st.zoom || st.panMode !== 'follow') return;

grep: one fast move from the centre

name: the pan is not clamped
why: Without the clamp a pointer in the edge zone or beyond the stage pans past the edge, opening a gap between the image and the frame.

edits.find: const axis = (p, start, size) => Math.max(-1, Math.min(1, (p - start - size / 2) / (size / 2 * reach)));
edits.replace: const axis = (p, start, size) => (p - start - size / 2) / (size / 2 * reach);

name: no edge zone
why: With a zone of 0 the edge shows only with the pointer on the stage's last pixel; a pointer 8 % in from it leaves 8 % of the overhang hidden.

name: no resize listener
why: The fit and the pan geometry are cached in px; after a resize, without a re-fit, the pan works from the old stage.

name: no fit at render, only on image load
why: Recorded as pass: the image's load event re-fits every image (thumbnail and large), even one the browser has cached, so no spec can see the render-time call. It is there so a remembered zoom applies at once on a step, without waiting for that load event.
